# The Evolution of Benchmarks in Frontier Models

**How the evaluations named in OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic model announcements change over time.**

[![CI](https://github.com/isingmodel/evolution_of_benchmarks_in_frontier_models/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/isingmodel/evolution_of_benchmarks_in_frontier_models/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Snapshot](https://img.shields.io/badge/observations_through-{{SNAPSHOT_BADGE}}-555)](#sample-and-method)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-3b7d44)](LICENSE)

Which kinds of tasks appear in each model's benchmark portfolio? How does that
mix change, which benchmarks become shared reference points, and which return
across later releases? This project connects a visual release history to a
source-linked catalog and reproducible analysis of each benchmark's reporting history.

**{{MODEL_ROWS}} model rows · {{LAUNCH_EVENTS}} distinct announcements · {{OBSERVED_BENCHMARKS}} observed benchmark identities · through {{AS_OF}}**

The evidence is **names appearing on selected public launch pages**: results,
comparisons, footnotes, suite components, and partner quotations all count.
Appearance does not by itself establish a score for the new model, prominence,
or use during training. Release discovery was checked through **October 4, 2026**.

## Benchmark types across model releases

This view connects **model, provider, release date, and benchmark composition**.
The five colors are a compact task-mode projection of the richer taxonomy:
Agentic, Multimodal Perception, Generative Reasoning, Constraint Satisfaction,
and Knowledge Retrieval.

![Model releases by actual date and provider, with benchmark task-mode composition](assets/benchmark_evolution.png)

Every model row is shown; selected names keep the overview readable.
The [fully labeled view](assets/benchmark_evolution_detail.png) identifies every row.
Read the colors as a summary of the tasks represented on each launch page.
These projected categories use provisional facets; “Agentic” is broader than the
explicit tool/environment interaction measure examined below. The
[release-view methods](analysis/benchmark_evolution/README.md) explain the visual
encoding and treatment of missing classifications.

## Benchmark types over time

The trailing **180-day** view brings out changes across release portfolios.
Each benchmark-bearing model row has one unit of weight, split across its
recorded resolved mentions. Repeated benchmark appearances contribute again;
this is composition of reporting, rather than a count of newly invented benchmarks.
Each window normalizes its covered category weight to 100%; windows without
covered observations remain gaps.

![Trailing 180-day task-mode composition of reported benchmark mentions](assets/benchmark_growth.png)

The curve is a descriptive taxonomy view. Sparse early releases and the mix of
providers affect it; classification gaps and provisional labels affect the
categories. The [task-mode and domain panels](assets/benchmark_growth_by_all_category.png)
and [multi-facet view](assets/benchmark_facet_trends.png) provide complementary
detail. See [trend methods](analysis/benchmark_taxonomy_trends/README.md) for the
window, denominator, and missing-data rules.

These two views retain **named model rows**, including jointly announced
variants. The sharing and lifecycle analyses below instead count each distinct
announcement once, and the interaction analysis compares both units.

## {{SHARING_TITLE}}

{{SHARING_FINDING}}
**{{SHARED_BENCHMARKS}} identities** appear at two or more providers;
**{{ALL_THREE_BENCHMARKS}}** appear at all three.

![Benchmark identities and reporting weight grouped by provider coverage](assets/benchmark_shared_core.png)

Giving each benchmark-bearing announcement one unit, divided across its canonical
benchmark set, shared identities contribute **{{SHARED_ANNOUNCEMENT_SHARE}}** of
the average portfolio. {{SHARING_WEIGHTING_INTERPRETATION}}

This result uses catalog identities: explicit versions remain separate, while
some historical rows combine variants. It does not establish benchmark-family
concentration or comparable scoring protocols.
[Counts and both weightings](analysis/project_overview/sharing_summary.csv).

## Each benchmark has a reporting history

{{SINGLETON_FINDING}}
Recent entries have less time to recur, so a single appearance is not a completed
lifetime. The lifecycle analysis follows first and last sightings, recurrence,
provider spread, and reporting gaps for every catalog identity.

![Selected benchmark histories with source-linked announcement dates](assets/benchmark_lifecycle.png)

Dots are actual announcement dates; grey spans connect first and last sightings
and can contain gaps. Last seen does not establish retirement, saturation, or
replacement. The [complete catalog report](analysis/benchmark_lifecycle/report.md)
covers **{{CATALOG_BENCHMARKS}} identities**, including **{{UNOBSERVED_BENCHMARKS}}**
unobserved by this cutoff. [Provider histories](analysis/benchmark_lifecycle/provider_lifecycles.csv)
count subsequent launches, including pages with no recorded benchmarks, so gaps
can be read against each provider's release cadence.

### How often does reporting spread to another provider?

The table includes identities that remain provider-specific, admitting each only when
the entire follow-up window fits inside the observed series.

{{DIFFUSION_TABLE}}

Each row has a different eligible cohort. Time starts at the first mention in
this dataset, rather than benchmark publication; an eligible window need not
contain another provider's launch. Follow-up ends at **{{DIFFUSION_FOLLOWUP_END}}**.
These are descriptive reporting fractions, not a survival curve or a field-wide
adoption probability.
[Window definitions and evidence](analysis/project_overview/README.md#diffusion-with-complete-calendar-follow-up).

## How much depends on the classification?

The overview also measures explicit interaction with tools or environments.
This narrower measure requires a tool, environment, browser, terminal/codebase,
or computer-control interaction label. Static code generation, unit-test scoring,
and planning alone do not qualify.

{{INTERACTION_SENSITIVITY_FINDING}}

The difference between all active labels and the rating-filtered view makes
annotation quality part of the result. A confidence rating of at least 0.70 is
a sensitivity filter, **not completed review**. Missing labels retain their
weight in the denominator; zero accepted-label coverage supplies no reviewed
basis for an estimate, rather than evidence that interaction is absent.

## Sample and method

There are **{{BENCHMARK_BEARING_LAUNCHES}} benchmark-bearing announcements** and
**{{LAUNCH_MENTIONS}} canonical benchmark–announcement observations**. The
announcement unit is a provider, release date, and normalized source URL;
aliases resolve through exact mappings.
[Annual inventory](analysis/project_overview/annual_inventory.csv) exposes uneven
coverage. [Overview methods](analysis/project_overview/README.md) define the
denominators and reconcile raw labels, model rows, and announcement observations.

Named suites and their components may both appear, so counts are not independent
tests. Some historical labels combine versions, and current launch pages can
have been edited since release. First sightings describe this sample, not
archived proof of when a benchmark entered public use.

The facet table contains **{{FACET_ROWS}} labels: {{FACET_ACCEPTED}} accepted,
{{FACET_NEEDS_REVIEW}} needing review, and {{FACET_LEGACY_SEED}} legacy seeds**.
Identity approval and facet approval are separate. The
[preface audit](docs/readme_data_audit_2026_10_04.md) records corrections including
MTOB's task definition and missing mentions, plus unresolved MRCR lineage. The
[release audit](docs/data_refresh_2026_10_04.md) records source-discovery coverage.

these open research questions; earlier analyses remain available for comparison.

## Reproduce and extend

Python **3.10–3.14** is tested in CI. From the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt -e .
.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests
bash scripts/run_pipeline.sh
```

The pipeline rebuilds tables, figures, and this README from committed inputs;
no model API credentials are needed. The cutoff defaults to the latest release
date; set `AS_OF=YYYY-MM-DD` to select another. CI checks deterministic text
outputs; PNG bytes can vary with fonts.

To extend the data, follow the [extraction and review workflow](docs/release_page_extraction_workflow.md)
and [data guide](data/README.md). Edit the preface in
[README.template.md](analysis/project_overview/README.template.md); its counts
and evidence tables are generated. Taxonomy reclassification is a separate
[authoring step](docs/benchmark_classification_prompt.md) whose current client
also depends on maintainer-local tooling.
